title: Your name for Him
hookLine: a name of Allah you turn to most
tomorrow: the First and the Last, hidden and seen. how is He both?

cards: Scroll through the contacts in a phone and you'll find someone saved as Mom, someone saved as a nickname only two people understand. The name you give someone says who they are to you.
Jordan spent the whole of moving day carrying boxes into Amira's house.
That night, eating takeout on the floor of Dadi's new room, she asked Dadi something nobody in the family had thought to ask: when it's just you, what do you call God? Dadi didn't have to think.

teach.b: "When I'm scared, Ya Latif. The Gentle, the Subtle. When I'm grateful, Ya Karim." Is that allowed, a favorite?

teach.h: HIS ARE THE MOST BEAUTIFUL NAMES.
teach.b: The Qur'an's answer comes in Surah al-Isra: call on Allah, or call on Ar-Rahman, the Beneficent, whichever you call, "His are the most beautiful names." A favorite name isn't a smaller God.
It's the door you know best into the same house. Then Jordan said her grandmother, at church and at the stove, just says Father. And here the two traditions stand side by side.

teach.h: ABBA, FATHER: A NAME FOR THE HOUR.
teach.b: In the Gospel of Mark, on the night of his arrest, Jesus prays in a garden, in the King James words: "Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee." A name that fits the hour, said by someone afraid.
Dadi's Ya Latif lives in that same place. Shared: in both, people in trouble reach for the name that fits the trouble.
And the honest difference. For Christians, Father is at the heart of prayer; Jesus taught them to begin "Our Father which art in heaven."

In Islam, Father is not among the Names. The Qur'an says "Naught is as His likeness," so Muslims call on Him by the Names He gave. Here's the thing to tell a friend: two grandmothers, two names, the same reach.

how: Muslims call on Allah with the Name that fits the need, Ya Rahman for mercy, Ya Latif in hardship, Ya Razzaq for provision, often within a du'a.

games.q: what does “your name for him” mean?
o: the Name you reach for first when it's just you
a secret name of God known only to the saints
a nickname for God that replaces the name Allah

p: Jesus in the garden, in Mark
His are the most beautiful names

s: Muslims may call on Allah only by the name Allah
the Qur'an says call on Allah or on the Beneficent, whichever: His are the most beautiful names.
in Mark's Gospel, Jesus prays 'Abba, Father' in the garden
"Abba, Father, all things are possible unto thee."

games.q: at an interfaith dinner, a guest smiles: 'all religions call God Father, right?' what's the honest answer?
o: Christians do, from the Lord's Prayer; in Islam, Father isn't among the Names.
yes, basically; every religion means the same thing by the word Father.
no; only Christians actually pray to God by any personal name at all.
games.why: both traditions reach for a name that fits the hour. the names themselves differ, and saying so plainly ranks no one.

practice: Write one Name by hand on a scrap of paper: the one you'd reach for this week, Ar-Rahman, Al-Latif, As-Sabur, any of them. If you pray, say it once, quietly; if not, write the quality you most need right now.
Sit with the paper in front of you.

wordCard.voice: Your name for Him: the Name you reach for first, a door into the One who has all of them.

orig.note: Arabic: the most beautiful Names, the Qur'an's phrase in 17:110 and 7:180.

carryVoice: Pocket this: my name for him, chosen from the ninety-nine, said in the dark when it's just me. The names, gathered, begin.
